narrative: The model estimated a 41% chance that you would become a bad credit risk. That is not a certainty, but under the bank’s conservative policy it is high enough to deny the loan. The strongest factor in the decision was your credit history, described as critical or other credits. Interestingly, this factor actually helped your case, pulling the risk estimate down. The denial was driven more by the second and third most important factors: your checking account status and your savings. Your checking balance is in the 0–200 DM range. Among approved applicants, most had no checking account or a stronger balance, and only about 18% shared your range, so the model saw less liquidity here and pushed toward bad credit. Your savings below 100 DM also added risk because it leaves little financial cushion. Together, these two liquidity signals outweighed the favorable credit-history effect and kept the estimated risk above the bank’s cutoff. To improve a future application, work on building savings above 100 DM, maintaining a healthier checking balance, resolving critical or other credit issues, and consider requesting a smaller amount or shorter term. You may also ask the bank for specific adverse-action reasons and explore a secured or co-signed loan.
